verdict.rationale: Gitea's automations are Gitea Actions workflows written as YAML. Gitea itself provides commit history plus Pull Request and AGit code review, so workflow definitions can be versioned and reviewed natively. However, the evidence never explicitly says workflow files live in the repository and are governed by these features, and nothing documents rollback of automations. Missing for 10: explicit documentation that workflow YAML is versioned in-repo, a documented rollback or revert path for automations, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can version, review, and roll back my automations

citations.quote: Users can write workflows in familiar YAML format and reuse a variety of existing Actions plugins.
browsing commit history and code files, reviewing and merging code submissions
Code review supports both the Pull Request workflow and AGit workflow.
